edges.effect_quant: Among BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers, risk-reducing mastectomy is associated with very large reductions in subsequent breast-cancer events, and several cohorts report no incident breast cancers during follow-up after prophylactic surgery.
edges.population: women carrying BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic variants considering or undergoing prophylactic mastectomy
edges.mechanism: Risk-reducing mastectomy removes the majority of breast epithelium at highest baseline genetic risk for malignant transformation. That direct tissue-removal mechanism explains why this edge behaves differently from chemoprevention or surveillance alone.
edges.summary: For BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers, prophylactic mastectomy is one of the clearest risk-reduction interventions in hereditary breast oncology. The best prospective and multi-centre cohort data show extremely low subsequent breast-cancer incidence after surgery, often with zero observed events during available follow-up.
edges.caveats: This edge is about cancer-risk reduction, not the full lived tradeoff of surgery. Surgical morbidity, reconstruction burden, body-image effects, and the possibility of residual breast tissue all matter in decision-making even when the oncologic signal is very strong.

evidence.notes: Association of risk-reducing surgery in BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation carriers with cancer risk and mortality.

evidence.citation: EvansDG et al 2009 J Med Genet
evidence.notes: Risk reducing mastectomy: outcomes in 10 European centres.
